title: Weekly semaglutide lowers body weight by about 15 percent in trial

passages: In the first study, involving 1,961 people, people treated with Wegovy were able to lose on average 15% of their weight after 68 weeks compared with a 2% loss of weight in people who had placebo (a dummy treatment).
In the second study, involving 611 people, those treated with Wegovy lost on average 16% of their body weight after 68 weeks compared with a 6% loss of weight in people who had placebo.
After 68 weeks, those treated with Wegovy were able on average to lose 10% of their weight compared with a 3% weight loss in people who had placebo.

In a study involving 307 adults who had obesity, or who were overweight and had at least one weight-related health problem, people taking Wegovy tablets for 64 weeks lost on average around 14% of their weight, compared with around 2% for those who received placebo.
Other information about Wegovy Wegovy received a marketing authorisation valid throughout the EU on 6 January 2022.
The study found that after 68 weeks, BMI dropped by an average of 16% in those treated with Wegovy compared with an average increase of less than 1% in those who received placebo.

After 48 more weeks, those who continued on Wegovy lost a further 8% of their weight while those on placebo regained 7% of theirs, indicating that people need to continue taking Wegovy in order not to regain weight.
Around 73% of those who received Wegovy lost at least 5% of their weight compared with around 18% of those who received placebo.
In addition, around 76% of people taking Wegovy tablets lost at least 5% of their weight, compared with around 31% of those who received placebo.
Around 85% of people in the Wegovy group lost at least 5% of their weight compared with 48% of people in the placebo group.

items.title_found: FDA Approves First Treatment to Reduce Risk of Serious Heart Problems Specifically in Adults with Obesity or Overweight
items.meta_description: The FDA approved a new use for a drug to reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease, heart attack and stroke in adults with cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight.
passages: Wegovy is also approved to reduce excess weight and maintain weight reduction long term in certain adults with obesity or overweight and certain children with obesity, for use in addition to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity.

Food and Drug Administration approved a new indication for use for Wegovy (semaglutide) injection to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack and stroke in adults with cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight.
Obesity and overweight are serious health issues that increase the risk for premature death and a variety of health problems, including heart attack and stroke.
Obesity or overweight affect approximately 70% of American adults.
Wegovy contains semaglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist.
Therefore, Wegovy should not be used in combination with other semaglutide-containing products or other GLP-1 receptor agonists.
Wegovy should not be used in patients with a history of a severe allergic reaction to semaglutide or to any of the other ingredients.

Wegovy significantly reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, heart attack and stroke), which occurred in 6.5% of participants who received Wegovy compared to 8% of participants who received placebo.

Wegovy also contains warnings for inflammation of the pancreas (pancreatitis), gallbladder problems (including gallstones), low blood sugar, acute kidney injury, hypersensitivity reactions, diabetic retinopathy (damage to the eye's retina), increased heart rate and suicidal behavior or thinking.

Wegovy’s efficacy and safety for this new indication were studied in a multi-national, multi-center, placebo-controlled double-blind trial that randomly assigned over 17,600 participants to receive either Wegovy or placebo.

passages: Clinical trials indicate that when used alongside diet, physical activity, and behavioural support, Wegovy users can achieve up to a 15% reduction in body weight after one year.
Wegovy is the brand name for semaglutide, which is licensed and approved for managing overweight and obesity.
To get Wegovy on the NHS, eligible adults would need a referral to an NHS specialist weight management service.
Semaglutide (Wegovy) for weight loss has only just launched in the UK and there are no known supply issues.
It is manufactured by Novo Nordisk and is recommended by the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) for managing overweight and obesity in some patients on the NHS.
NICE’s final guidance will support the NHS in identifying the most effective digital technologies where digital weight management services are considered appropriate for meeting local need.
NICE determine the eligibility criteria for routine use of Wegovy on the NHS to ensure value for money for the NHS.
NHS England is legally required to make Wegovy available to NHS patients in line with NICE’s recommendations within 3 months of its commercial availability.
Wegovy is for those dealing with obesity and weight-related problems, not for people who just want to lose some weight.
Whether you get Wegovy from the NHS or privately, the prescribers need to follow professional guidelines and consider national advice.
